title: PreGIP: Watermarking the Pretraining of Graph Neural Networks for Deep IP Protection

problem.claim: Pretrained GNNs are valuable intellectual property because pretraining requires substantial data and computational resources, but adversaries may copy and deploy them.

gap.claim: Existing GNN watermarking methods target classifiers and are not applicable to self-supervised GNN pretraining.

contributions.claim: PreGIP is a framework for watermarking GNN encoder pretraining for IP protection while maintaining embedding-space quality.
PreGIP uses a task-free watermarking loss to watermark the embedding space of a pretrained GNN encoder.
PreGIP deploys a finetuning-resistant watermark injection.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe PreGIP as a novel framework for watermarking GNN pretraining.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theoretical analysis and extensive experiments show PreGIP's effectiveness.
The authors provide code through two anonymous repository links.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNN pretraining supports various downstream tasks.
The cost of pretraining makes pretrained GNNs valuable IP vulnerable to unauthorized copying and deployment.
Existing watermarking methods for GNN classifiers do not address self-supervised GNN pretraining.
PreGIP watermarking combines a task-free embedding-space loss with finetuning-resistant injection.
The authors report theoretical analysis, extensive experiments, and released code.

source_observation.claim: The paper addresses a protection gap created by applying classifier watermarking methods to self-supervised pretraining settings.

interpretation.claim: Protection mechanisms may need to target the representation-learning stage rather than only downstream task models.

application.claim: For valuable pretrained encoders, consider watermarking the embedding space and evaluating resistance to later finetuning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported approach generalizes beyond the evaluated GNN pretraining setting.

unknowns: Watermark construction, injection procedure, and detection protocol are unspecified.
Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative experimental results are unspecified.
Threat model and finetuning conditions are unspecified.
Theoretical assumptions and analysis results are unspecified.
